Anya: Observed a ~12% p99 latency regression on mistral-8x7b after the kernel prefetch change when running sliding-window workloads where the attention mask toggles frequently. Repro on perf-cluster-2.
Devon: Can you drop the perf trace and a minimal repro? Is this only 8x7b or do we see it on 7b too?
Marta: Quick baseline profiling attached. Looks like the prefetch path picks a tiled matmul variant that thrashes KV tile boundaries when mask chunks flip.
Marta: ```
kernel: prefetched_tiled_matmul
pattern: sliding_window (seq chunks 256 / window 2048)
kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.18
p99: 86ms -> 96ms (after prefetch change)
```
Sam: Hypothesis: selector uses avg seq len but not mask sparsity. When mask toggles, memory access becomes non-contiguous and prefetching causes extra evictions. We should consider mask density variance in the selector.
Anya: I tried a tiny selector tweak locally: prefer_nonprefetch when mask_has_gaps=true. Locally p99 went from 96ms -> 83ms on the same trace.
Anya: Patch snippet: ```
if (mask_has_gaps && seq_window < 512) select(kernel_contiguous);
else select(kernel_prefetch);
```
Marta: Profiling also shows KV pointer churn — poswrap handling for 8x7b resets kv_ptr on mask shifts, which exacerbates reuse loss. Might be separate bug in max_position_embeddings handling.
Devon: Can you paste the smallest failing input and the config (rope_scale, max_pos, heads/kvdim)? I want a canary test.
Marta: Failing config: model=mistral-8x7b, rope_scale=0.9, max_pos=2048, heads=32, kv_dim=128. Input pattern toggles mask every 256 tokens.
perf-bot: perfbot: trace uploaded: https://perf.redwood/trace/1836509123-8x7b
Sam: Short-term mitigation: disable kernel prefetch for Mistral variants when sliding_window=true OR rope_scale != 1.0. Add selector guard: skip_prefetch_on_mask_sparsity.
Anya: I'll open a PR with the selector guard + unit test for mask patterns. Also adding an Optimize eval to catch >5% p99 regressions for these configs.
Marta: I'll add a regression test in the runtime CI that replays the uploaded trace and asserts p99 stays within 5% of baseline.
Devon: Thanks — if the PR looks good, add a rollback note and gate in canary. We should avoid surprising prod regressions.
Anya: :thumbsup: filing PR now, will call out the kv_ptr/poswrap follow-up in the description.
Sam: Long-term: we need the kernel selector to consider (mask_variance, rope_scale, kv_tile_alignment) and the runtime to expose kv reuse metrics so Optimize can suggest quant/tiling profiles.
Marta: Agreed. I'll start a short doc for selector heuristics and an instrumentation plan.
Anya: Closing loop: will post PR link when ready and ping here for canary run.
